xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:DisclosureOfNotesOnFinancialRe: Financial results have been prepared as per Ind AS prescribed under sec 133 of the Cos Act with Rule 3 of the Companies (IAS) Rules & amendments thereafter. Above financial results for the for quarter ended September 30,25 reviewed by AC & approved by BOD on 29.10.25 subject to LR by statutory auditors. Company engaged primarily in the business of operating private FM radio stations which constitutes single reportable segment.Accordingly Co. is single segment Co. in accordance with IAS 108 Operating Segments. Sec 115BAA of the IT Act 1961 provides an option to pay tax at 22% plus surcharge and cess subject to complying with certain conditions. Based on the assessment of future taxable profits Co. decided to continue with the existing rate until MAT credit balance is utilised and opt for the New Rate thereafter. The management measures its deferred tax balance at the end of each reporting period accordingly. Petition under sec 241, 242 and 244 of the Cos Act has been filed with NCLT on July 10, 23 by Mahendra Mohan Gupta Non-Executive Chairman & Promoter of JPL the Holding Co. & Shailesh Gupta WTD & member of the Promoter Group of Holding Co. & NED in their individual capacities against the other Promoters and members of the Promoter Group of the Holding Co. Litigation is currently pending at NCLT & several submissions have been made by all parties to the NCLT. As of this date the Co. does not expect any impact of this matter on its financial position as at September 30,25 and its future operations. During the year ended Mar 31,24 in the matter of the Co. vs PPL and other music providers the Hon’ble High Court of Madras partly allowed the appeal of PPL and other appellants by providing a minimum floor rate of Rs 660 per needle hour payable to PPL and other appellants for the use of sound recordings by the Co. over its radio stations in the past decade 2010-2020. The Co. has filed a special leave petition before the Hon’ble SC of India challenging the HC judgement. Further PPL had filed a contempt petition against the Co. and its directors and KMPs with the HC of Judicature at Madras alleging contempt of the order dated Apr 27, 23 which was heard by the HC and an order dated July 31, 24 was issued directing the Co. to deposit 50% of the amount projected in their grounds of appeal in the SLP filed in the Hon'ble SC of India i.e. Rs 1550 lakhs. An appeal was filed by the Co. before the Division Bench of HC on Aug 9,24 and the HC vide its interim order dated Sep 5, 24 has granted a stay against the above-mentioned demand order. Based on the opinion of external legal counsel and its internal assessment the Co. has a good case on merits and therefore the Co. does not expect outflow of any economic resources in this matter. The BOD had declared interim dividend for financial year ended Mar 31, 25 of Rs 0.01 per NCRPS ie. 0.1% of the face value of Rs. 10 each of NCRPS which was paid on Feb 17,25 to all the NCRPS holders whose names appear in the Register of Members of NCRPS as on the record date i.e. Jan7,25. During the year ended Mar 31,25 the Co. computed the value in use of its net assets and the said value was lower than the carrying value of its net assets by Rs 3492.99 lakhs. Accordingly the impairment loss of Rs 3492.99 lakhs was provided in financial results during the year ended Mar 31,25.
